en: to take a lesson; to model

examples.ko: 이번 실수를 거울삼아 다음에는 더 조심할게요.
examples.en: I'll learn from this mistake and be more careful next time.
Take your senior's experience as a lesson.
People who learn from failure end up succeeding.
You should learn from the past and prepare for the future.

examples.ko: 회사는 그 사고를 거울삼아서 안전 규칙을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The company took that accident as a lesson and changed its safety rules.

examples.ko: 남의 잘못도 거울삼으면 많이 배울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you learn even from others' mistakes, you can gain a lot.

explain: '~을/를 거울삼아'의 꼴로 가장 많이 쓰고, 지난 일이나 남의 일에서 교훈을 얻는다는 뜻이에요. '교훈으로 삼다'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 글 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Taking the past as a lesson, let's move forward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어가 가장 많이 쓰이는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of the headword.

phrases.en: I took my older brother's mistake as a lesson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 교훈을 얻었다고 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense, for when a lesson has already been drawn.

phrases.en: I'll take this failure as a lesson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 쉽고 말하는 느낌이 나는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more conversational way to say it.

explain_en: It is most often used in the form '~을/를 거울삼아', meaning to draw a lesson from past events or others' experiences. It is close to '교훈으로 삼다' but sounds a bit more written.

en: to make a firm decision; to decide resolutely

examples.en: The boss made a firm decision and chose to move the factory.
Now is really the time to make up your mind.

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 고민 끝에 회사를 떠나기로 결단했어요.
examples.en: After long deliberation, he resolved to leave the company.

examples.ko: 어려운 순간에는 빨리 결단하는 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: In hard moments, you need someone who decides quickly.
Mom resolved to move to a bigger hospital.
I did not have the courage to decide, so I kept putting it off.

explain: 오래 망설이다가 마음을 굳게 정하는 큰 결정이에요. 점심 메뉴를 정할 때는 '결정하다'를 쓰고, 직장을 그만두거나 이사를 가는 것처럼 용기가 필요한 선택에 결단하다를 써요. '결단을 내리다'라는 말도 자주 해요.

phrases.en: After long thought, I made a firm decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결단하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자주 들리는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 결단하다 and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Leaving the company was a big decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결단'을 명사로 써서 용기가 필요한 선택을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 결단 as a noun for a choice that takes courage.

phrases.en: Our team leader is decisive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨리 마음을 정하는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a person who decides firmly.

explain_en: It is a big decision made firmly after hesitating for a long time. For choosing a lunch menu you use '결정하다', and 결단하다 fits choices that need courage, like quitting a job or moving. '결단을 내리다' is also a common phrase.

p.n: 결단하다 stresses a firm, brave decision; 결정하다 is neutral.

examples.en: The child fell and wailed.
Everyone sobbed loudly at the end of the movie.

examples.ko: 친구가 이별 얘기를 하며 꺼이꺼이 울더라고요.
examples.en: My friend bawled while talking about the breakup.

examples.ko: 그는 합격 소식에 꺼이꺼이 소리 내어 울었어요.
examples.en: He cried out loud, sobbing, at the news that he passed.
I could hear loud sobbing from the next room.

examples.ko: 꺼이꺼이 울고 나니까 마음이 좀 가벼워졌어요.
examples.en: After sobbing my heart out, I felt a bit lighter.

explain: 거의 '울다'와 함께 쓰고, 목이 메어 숨을 끊어 가며 크게 우는 소리를 나타내요. '엉엉'은 소리 내어 크게 우는 모양이고, '꺼이꺼이'는 목이 메어 울음이 끊기는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 이별 소식을 듣고 친구가 꺼이꺼이 울었어요.
phrases.en: My friend heard about the breakup and sobbed loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 부사와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요. 목이 메어 크게 우는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for this adverb. It describes crying loudly with a choked voice.

phrases.example: 졸업식에서 선생님을 보자 꺼이꺼이 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
phrases.en: I burst into loud sobs when I saw my teacher at the graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참고 있던 울음이 갑자기 터져 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when held-back tears suddenly burst out.

phrases.en: The child lost a toy and cried loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '엉엉'은 소리 내어 크게 우는 모양이고, '꺼이꺼이'는 울음이 끊기는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but '엉엉' is loud wailing, while '꺼이꺼이' has more of a choked, broken sound.

explain_en: It is used almost only with '울다' and describes crying hard with a choked voice, breaking for breath. '엉엉' is loud crying in general, while '꺼이꺼이' stresses the choked, broken sound.

examples.ko: 이번 시험에 떨어지고 나서 다시금 마음을 다잡았어요.
examples.en: After failing this exam, I pulled myself together once more.
I will steady my scattered mind and start studying.
You have to keep your focus to avoid mistakes.
I take a walk every morning to steady my mind.
Since it is a new year, I decided to renew my resolve.
The team leader pulled the wavering team back together.

explain: '마음을 다잡다'가 가장 흔한 쓰임이고, 정신, 자세, 분위기 같은 말과도 같이 써요. 흐트러진 것을 다시 단단히 바로잡는 느낌이라, 그냥 '잡다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I failed, but I steadied my mind and started again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 쓰임으로, 흔들린 마음을 바로잡는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, meaning to regain composure after wavering.

phrases.en: I felt sleepy, so I pulled myself together and studied.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집중이 흐트러졌을 때 다시 정신을 차린다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of regaining focus when concentration slips.

phrases.en: I straightened up my posture before the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸가짐이나 태도를 다시 단정히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tidying up one's bearing or attitude again.

explain_en: The most common use is '마음을 다잡다', and it also goes with words like spirit, posture and atmosphere. It feels like firmly re-steadying something that had loosened, which differs from plain '잡다'.

en: to recover one's composure; to settle

examples.en: This time I'm going to settle down and try studying properly.

examples.ko: 그는 다시 마음잡아 새 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: He pulled himself together and started a new job.

examples.ko: 시험이 가까워지면 마음잡아야 하는데 자꾸 놀게 돼요.
examples.en: I should buckle down as the exam gets closer, but I keep playing around.
It took my younger sibling a while to settle down.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝났는데도 마음잡지 못하고 놀기만 해요.
examples.en: The exam is over, but I still can't settle down and just keep playing around.
I'm so relieved to hear my friend has gotten himself together.

explain: 들뜨거나 흔들리던 마음을 가라앉히고 한 가지 일에 자리 잡을 때 써요. '마음(을) 잡다'로 띄어 쓰기도 하고, 반대로는 '마음을 못 잡다'라고 많이 말해요. '정신 차리다'는 잘못을 깨닫는 느낌이 강하고, 마음잡다는 차분히 자리 잡는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I settled my mind and started exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 다른 행동이 이어지는 연결형으로, 굳게 마음먹고 한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking form that leads into another action, with a feeling of firm resolve.

phrases.example: 이번에는 마음을 잡고 한국어를 공부할 거예요.
phrases.en: This time I'll settle down and study Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 띄어 쓴 형태로 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form, often used in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 이사한 뒤로 마음을 못 잡고 있어요.
phrases.en: I haven't been able to settle down since moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 안정되지 않을 때 쓰는 반대 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite expression, for when your mind won't settle.

explain_en: It is used when someone calms a restless or wavering mind and settles on one thing. It is also written as '마음(을) 잡다' with a space, and the opposite is usually '마음을 못 잡다'. '정신 차리다' stresses realizing a mistake, while 마음잡다 feels like calmly settling down.

en: to be immersed in; to be absorbed in

examples.en: When I read a book, I get completely absorbed.
He got so absorbed in the game that he forgot to eat.

examples.ko: 일에 몰입하는 사람은 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: For people absorbed in their work, time goes fast.
Please turn off your phone so you can get into the movie.
The child was absorbed in drawing.

examples.ko: 몰입할 수 있는 취미가 있으면 좋아요.
examples.en: It is nice to have a hobby you can lose yourself in.

explain: 보통 '~에 몰입하다'로 써요. '집중하다'는 눈앞의 일에 주의를 모으는 것이고, '몰입하다'는 시간이 가는 줄 모를 만큼 깊이 빠지는 느낌이에요. '빠지다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I can get absorbed in this movie easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '몰입'과 함께 써서 푹 빠지는 정도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '몰입' to describe how absorbed you get.

phrases.en: Before an exam, I focus on studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰입하다'보다 가볍게 주의를 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for focusing attention more lightly than '몰입하다'.

phrases.en: These days I'm hooked on a drama.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '몰입하다' 대신 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural everyday alternative to '몰입하다'.

explain_en: It is usually used as '~에 몰입하다'. '집중하다' means gathering your attention on what is in front of you; '몰입하다' means being so deep in it that you lose track of time. It is a bit more formal than '빠지다'.

examples.en: Everyone burst into hearty laughter at the comedy act.
The whole family roars with laughter at my friend's joke.
The sound of roaring laughter was heard in the next room.
It was a story so funny that even the teacher would roar with laughter.
It was so funny that I laughed out loud until tears came.

examples.ko: 그 장면을 떠올리면 박장대소할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: When I think of that scene, I can't help but burst out laughing.

explain: 손뼉을 치면서 크게 웃는다는 한자 그대로의 모습이 떠오르는 말이에요. 여럿이 함께 있을 때 잘 어울려요. '폭소하다'는 웃음이 갑자기 터지는 데 초점이 있고, '박장대소하다'는 크게 웃는 모습 자체에 초점이 있어요.

phrases.example: 친구들이 그 장면을 보고 박장대소를 했어요.
phrases.en: My friends burst into loud laughter at that scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박장대소하다'를 '명사 + 하다' 꼴로 나눠 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb split into 'noun + 하다' form.

phrases.en: We all took photos while laughing out loud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형으로 써서 웃으면서 다른 행동을 한다고 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: In its connective form, it lets you say you did something else while laughing.

phrases.en: The audience burst into laughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음이 갑자기 터지는 순간에 초점이 있어서 '박장대소'와 조금 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the sudden burst of laughter, which differs slightly from '박장대소'.

explain_en: It brings to mind the literal picture of clapping while laughing loudly, and it fits best when several people are together. '폭소하다' focuses on laughter suddenly bursting out, while '박장대소하다' focuses on the picture of laughing big.

examples.en: The hero's name will remain immortal.
People dream of immortality but cannot achieve it.
It is a song called an immortal masterpiece.
The word immortal suits this artist.

examples.ko: 이 탑은 사랑의 불멸을 상징한다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this tower symbolizes the immortality of love.

examples.ko: 이야기 속 왕은 불멸의 약을 찾아 떠났어요.
examples.en: In the story, the king set out to find the elixir of immortality.

explain: 죽지 않고 영원히 남는다는 느낌이라 '불멸의 명곡', '불멸의 사랑'처럼 '불멸의 + 명사'로 많이 써요. '영원'은 끝이 없다는 느낌이고, '불멸'은 죽음이나 사라짐을 이겨낸다는 점이 달라요. 이야기, 시, 영화에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That hero remained as an immortal name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사라지지 않고 오래 기억되는 이름을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a name that is remembered forever.

phrases.en: This film is an immortal masterpiece.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜 시간이 지나도 사랑받는 작품에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for works loved through the ages.

phrases.en: That story portrayed an immortal love.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시나 영화에서 끝나지 않는 사랑을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in poems and films for a love that never ends.

explain_en: It is mostly used as 불멸의 + noun, such as 불멸의 명곡 or 불멸의 사랑. 영원 stresses having no end, while 불멸 stresses overcoming death or disappearance. It often appears in stories, poems and films.

examples.ko: 주말에 집에서 푹 쉴 수 있다니 상팔자네요.
examples.en: You get to rest at home all weekend? Lucky you.

examples.ko: 일 안 하고 쉬는 친구가 상팔자로 보여요.
examples.en: My friend who's resting and not working looks like he has it easy.

examples.ko: 매일 늦잠 자는 고양이가 제일 상팔자예요.
examples.en: The cat that sleeps in every day has the best life.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 이불 속에 있으면 그게 상팔자죠.
examples.en: Being under the blanket on a rainy day, that's the good life.

examples.ko: 요즘 아이들이 학원에 안 가면 상팔자라고 하더라고요.
examples.en: These days they say kids who skip cram school have it made.

examples.ko: 월급 받으면서 놀 수 있다니 상팔자 아니에요?
examples.en: Getting paid while you play, isn't that the easy life?

explain: 걱정 없이 편하게 지내는 사람의 처지를 부러워하거나 가볍게 투덜거릴 때 써요. 주로 '~가 상팔자다', '~가 상팔자네요'처럼 말해요. 진지한 칭찬보다는 일상 대화에서 농담처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요.

phrases.example: 저는 야근하는데 강아지는 하루 종일 자네요. 개 팔자가 상팔자예요.
phrases.en: I'm working overtime and the puppy sleeps all day. That dog has it made.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나는 바쁘고 힘든데 편히 쉬는 대상이 부러울 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb you say when you are busy and envy someone, or some animal, who gets to relax.
phrases.en_equiv: must be nice; living the life

explain_en: You use it to envy, or gently grumble about, someone who lives an easy, carefree life. It usually appears as '~가 상팔자다' or '~가 상팔자네요'. It is more of a casual, joking remark than serious praise.

examples.en: How nice would it be if everything in life went my way?
My grandfather is interested in everything under the sun.

examples.ko: 가끔은 세상만사가 다 귀찮을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel bothered by everything in the world.
They say everything depends on your state of mind, don't they?

examples.ko: 퇴근하고 나니 세상만사가 다 편안해 보여요.
examples.en: After leaving work, everything in the world looks peaceful.

examples.ko: 친구랑 세상만사 이야기를 하다 보니 밤이 깊었어요.
examples.en: Talking about all sorts of things with my friend, the night grew late.

explain: '세상의 모든 일'이라는 뜻이라서 '세상만사가 귀찮다', '세상만사 다 잊고 쉬고 싶다'처럼 지치거나 편안한 기분을 말할 때 자주 써요. '세상만사 마음먹기에 달렸다'는 한 덩어리로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: These days everything feels like a bother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지치고 의욕이 없을 때 쓰는 대표 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard expression for when you feel tired and unmotivated.

phrases.en: Everything in life depends on your mindset.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 덩어리로 외워서 마음가짐이 중요하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed phrase used to say that mindset is what matters.

phrases.example: 세상 모든 일이 마음대로 되지는 않아요.
phrases.en: Not everything in the world goes the way you want.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세상만사'를 쉽게 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, spelled-out way to say 세상만사.

explain_en: It covers all the affairs of the world, so people use it to express moods, as in '세상만사가 귀찮다' (I'm sick of everything) or '세상만사 다 잊고 쉬고 싶다' (I want to forget everything and rest). The saying '세상만사 마음먹기에 달렸다' is also often used as a set phrase.

examples.ko: 마음 수양을 위해 매일 아침 명상을 해요.
examples.en: I meditate every morning to cultivate my mind.
He is someone who has cultivated himself all his life.

examples.ko: 수양이 부족해서 작은 일에도 화를 내요.
examples.en: I lack self-discipline, so I get angry even over small things.
Self-cultivation takes a lot of time and effort.
I spent time on self-cultivation at a temple in the mountains.

examples.ko: 이 책은 인격 수양에 도움이 되는 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: This book has many stories that help build character.

explain: 몸보다 마음과 인격을 닦는다는 점이 중심이라서 '마음 수양', '인격 수양', '수양을 쌓다'처럼 말해요. 기술이나 무예를 익힐 때는 '수련'을 쓰고, '수양버들'의 수양은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: He quietly cultivated his mind in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수양'의 동사형으로, 마음과 인격을 닦는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '수양', meaning to cultivate mind and character.

phrases.en: Reading helps with character building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람됨을 닦는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for refining one's character.

phrases.example: 그는 매일 새벽에 무예 수련을 해요.
phrases.en: He trains in martial arts every dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기술이나 무예를 익힐 때는 '수양' 대신 '수련'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '수련' instead of '수양' for practicing a skill or martial art.

explain_en: The focus is on training the mind and character rather than the body, so people say '마음 수양', '인격 수양' and '수양을 쌓다'. For learning a skill or martial art, '수련' is used, and the 수양 in '수양버들' (weeping willow) is a different word.

examples.ko: 할머니의 슬기 덕분에 어려운 시기를 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my grandmother's wisdom, we got through hard times.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 우리가 슬기를 모아서 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: We have to pool our wisdom to solve this.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 슬기가 남달라서 어른들도 놀랐어요.
examples.en: That child had such rare good sense that even adults were surprised.

examples.ko: 옛사람들의 슬기를 배울 수 있는 책이에요.
examples.en: It's a book where you can learn the wisdom of people of old.
He showed good sense in the crisis and saved everyone.

examples.ko: 슬기와 용기가 있으면 두려울 게 없어요.
examples.en: With wisdom and courage, there's nothing to fear.

explain: '지혜'와 거의 같지만 '슬기'는 어려운 상황을 잘 풀어 가는 실제적인 재치에 더 가까워요. '슬기롭다'로 자주 쓰고, '슬기를 발휘하다', '슬기를 모으다'처럼 함께 써요.

phrases.en: She solved the problem wisely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '슬기'에서 나온 형용사로, '슬기롭게' 꼴로 행동을 꾸미는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form of the word, often used as 'wisely' to describe an action.

phrases.en: He showed good sense in the crisis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 순간에 재치 있게 잘 해낸다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning handling a hard moment with good sense.

phrases.en: A wise person stays calm in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지식이 많은 사람보다 상황을 잘 풀어 가는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone good at handling situations rather than someone with lots of knowledge.

explain_en: Nearly the same as 지혜, but 슬기 leans toward the practical cleverness of handling difficult situations well. It often appears as 슬기롭다 and in phrases like 슬기를 발휘하다 and 슬기를 모으다.

examples.en: Maybe I have itchy feet; I want to go off somewhere.

examples.ko: 그는 역마살 때문에 늘 여행을 다녀요.
examples.en: He is always traveling because of his wanderlust.

examples.ko: 엄마는 제 역마살을 말릴 수가 없다고 하세요.
examples.en: My mom says she can't stop my wanderlust.

examples.ko: 우리 아빠의 역마살은 친척들 사이에서도 유명해요.
examples.en: My dad's wanderlust is famous even among our relatives.

examples.ko: 역마살도 타고난 거라서 어쩔 수 없대요.
examples.en: They say wanderlust is something you're born with, so it can't be helped.
I was told that my fortune chart has the wanderer's fate.

explain: 원래는 사주에서 한곳에 못 있고 떠돌아다니는 운을 말하는데, 요즘은 여행을 좋아하고 가만히 못 있는 사람을 농담처럼 말할 때 많이 써요. '역마살이 끼다/있다'처럼 말해요. 나쁜 뜻이 아니라 가볍게 놀리는 느낌으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 저는 역마살이 있어서 한곳에 오래 못 있어요.
phrases.en: I have wanderlust, so I can't stay in one place long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행을 좋아하고 가만히 못 있는 사람을 가볍게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lightly describes someone who loves to travel and can't stay put.

phrases.example: 올해는 역마살이 끼었는지 자꾸 출장을 가요.
phrases.en: I keep going on business trips this year, as if I've got wanderlust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 돌아다니게 될 때 농담처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used jokingly when you end up moving around a lot.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 역마살이 세서 늘 비행기를 타요.
phrases.en: My friend has strong wanderlust and is always on a plane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 성향이 아주 강하다고 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Teasingly says that the tendency is very strong.

explain_en: Originally it is the fate of wandering that a fortune chart shows, but today people often use it jokingly for someone who loves travel and can't sit still. It appears as '역마살이 끼다/있다'. It is often a light tease rather than a negative word.

examples.ko: 그는 성격이 염세적이라 늘 세상을 어둡게 봐요.
examples.en: He is world-weary by nature, so he always sees the world as dark.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 전체적으로 염세적 분위기가 강해요.
examples.en: This novel has a strongly pessimistic mood overall.

examples.ko: 요즘 뉴스를 너무 봐서 염세적으로 변했어요.
examples.en: I watched too much news lately and became cynical about the world.
When I read a gloomy, world-weary poem, my mood sinks.
My brother used to be world-weary, but he brightened up after finding a hobby.
Even people who aren't world-weary get tired sometimes.

explain: '비관적'은 앞일을 어둡게 보는 것이고, 염세적은 세상이나 삶 자체에 싫증을 느끼는 쪽이에요. 반대말로는 '낙천적'을 써요. '염세적인', '염세적으로'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 염세적인 사람이라 늘 불평이 많아요.
phrases.en: He is a world-weary person, so he complains a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상에 싫증을 느끼는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who is tired of the world.

phrases.en: He views the world pessimistically.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상이나 삶을 어둡게 바라보는 태도를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gloomy attitude toward the world or life.

phrases.en: These days I often have pessimistic thoughts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶이 의미 없다는 듯한 생각을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for thoughts that life feels meaningless.

explain_en: '비관적' means seeing the future in a dark light, while 염세적 is weariness with the world or life itself. Its opposite is '낙천적'. It is used with endings like '염세적인' and '염세적으로'.

examples.en: They lost their child, so how frightened they must have been.
To cry like that, how hard it must have been.
Having failed the exam, how upset must she be?
Living alone in a strange place, he must be so lonely.
How urgent it must have been for him to run off like that.

examples.ko: 아침도 못 먹고 일했으니 오죽이나 배고팠겠어요.
examples.en: He worked without breakfast, so he must have been so hungry.

explain: 뒤에 '-겠어요', '-ㄹ까요'가 와서 상대의 힘든 처지를 헤아릴 때 써요. '오죽'이나 '오죽하면'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: How awful the parents must have felt when they lost their child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-했겠어요'로 끝내서 상대의 마음을 헤아릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ending with '-했겠어요' to show you understand how someone felt.
phrases.en_equiv: how hard it must have been

phrases.en: He must have been desperate to go that far.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정말 어쩔 수 없어서'라는 뜻으로, 이유를 이해해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means 'it must have been unavoidable', showing understanding of a reason.

phrases.en: Raising a child alone must be so hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이나'를 빼고 짧게 말하면 더 자연스러운 입말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dropping '이나' makes it sound like more natural speech.

explain_en: It is followed by '-겠어요' or '-ㄹ까요' when you imagine how hard someone's situation is. '오죽' and '오죽하면' are used in a similar way.

en: to endure; to persevere; to be patient

examples.ko: 힘든 시간을 인내하면 좋은 날이 와요.
examples.en: If you endure the hard times, good days will come.

examples.ko: 오랜 시간 동안 아픔을 인내해 왔어요.
examples.en: I have borne the pain for a long time.

examples.ko: 선수는 부상을 인내하고 경기를 끝까지 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The player put up with the injury and played the match to the end.
You have to be very patient to raise a child.
They say that people who endure eventually succeed.

examples.ko: 더는 인내할 수 없어서 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: I could not stand it any longer, so I got angry.

explain: 말할 때는 '참다'를 많이 쓰고, '인내하다'는 글이나 연설에서 쓰는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 명사 '인내'는 '인내심'이라는 말로 더 자주 보여요. '인내심을 가지다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 인내심을 가지고 조금만 더 기다려 보세요.
phrases.en: Be patient and wait a little longer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인내하다'보다 말과 글에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common collocation than the verb 인내하다 in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: Even if it hurts, hold on a little longer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인내하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 말할 때 쓰는 쉽고 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 인내하다, but an easier, more everyday word for speaking.

phrases.en: She waited patiently for a good result.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 참으면서 다른 행동을 계속한다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connector -며 adds the idea of enduring while continuing another action.

explain_en: In speech people mostly say 참다; 인내하다 is a slightly stiff word for writing and speeches. The noun 인내 is more often seen as 인내심. A common phrase is '인내심을 가지다'.

en: path of life; course of life; journey of life

examples.en: A person's life path is long and far, like a marathon.

examples.ko: 부모님은 제 인생길을 늘 응원해 주세요.
examples.en: My parents always support my path in life.
Even on a rough road of life, my friend was by my side.
The road of life has both uphills and downhills.

examples.ko: 저는 이제 새로운 인생길을 걷기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I have now started walking a new path in life.

examples.ko: 그 선택은 제 인생길을 완전히 바꿔 놓았어요.
examples.en: That choice completely changed the course of my life.

explain: 인생을 걸어가는 길에 빗댄 말이라 노래, 편지, 연설에서 자주 나와요. '인생길을 걷다', '험한 인생길'처럼 말하고, 평소 대화에서는 그냥 '인생'이라고 해도 충분해요.

phrases.example: 저는 제 인생길을 천천히 걷고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm walking my own path of life slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶을 길에 빗대어 말하는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase comparing life to a road.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk the path of life

phrases.en: Even a rough path of life is okay when we walk it together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 삶을 표현할 때 노래나 편지에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in songs and letters to express a hard life.

phrases.en: My husband is my companion on life's journey.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평생 함께하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who stays with you for life.

explain_en: It pictures life as a road you walk, so it shows up often in songs, letters and speeches. Typical uses are '인생길을 걷다' and '험한 인생길'. In ordinary conversation, plain '인생' is usually enough.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 처세술이 좋아서 어디서든 잘 지내요.
examples.en: He's good at getting along, so he does well anywhere.
I think social skills are needed in working life too.

examples.ko: 처세술에 관한 책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a book about social savvy.
Is flattering people also a kind of social tactic?

examples.ko: 그는 말하는 법부터 처세술까지 선배에게 배웠어요.
examples.en: He learned everything from how to speak to how to handle people from his senior.

examples.ko: 처세술만 믿고 실력은 키우지 않으면 오래가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you rely only on social tactics and don't build skill, it's hard to last.

explain: 세상을 살아가면서 사람들과 잘 지내는 기술이에요. '요령'은 일을 쉽게 하는 비결이고, 처세술은 사람을 대하는 방법에 쓰는 말이에요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓸 때도 있지만 계산적이라는 느낌이 들어갈 때도 있어요. 예를 들어 윗사람에게 잘 보이려는 행동을 '처세술'이라고 부르면 조금 비꼬는 말이 돼요.

phrases.en: He is very good at getting along with people, so he's popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 대하는 솜씨가 좋다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone is skilled in dealing with people.
phrases.en_equiv: to be skilled at worldly wisdom

phrases.en: I learned how to get along in society from this book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회생활에서 필요한 방법을 익힌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means picking up the skills needed in social life.

phrases.en: I bought a book on social savvy at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람과 잘 지내는 법을 다룬 책을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a book about getting along with people.

explain_en: It is the skill of living in society and getting along with people. '요령' is a knack for getting a job done easily, while 처세술 is about how you deal with people. It can be positive, but sometimes it feels calculating. Calling an effort to impress superiors '처세술' can sound a bit sarcastic.

examples.en: My grandmother believes that after death one goes to heaven.
They say if you live a good life, you go to heaven.
Soaking in the hot spring, this feels like heaven.
I heard a story about heaven and hell at church.

examples.ko: 천당에 가려고 착한 일을 하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: I don't do good deeds in order to go to heaven.
The child asked, 'Where is heaven?'

explain: 종교에서 좋은 사람이 죽은 뒤에 간다고 믿는 곳을 말하고, 반대말은 '지옥'이에요. '천국'이라고도 하고, 일상에서는 아주 편하고 좋은 곳을 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 좋은 일을 많이 하면 천국에 간대요.
phrases.en: They say you go to heaven if you do many good deeds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천당과 같은 뜻의 말이고 더 널리 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more widely used.

phrases.en: A room with air conditioning feels like heaven.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 편하고 좋은 곳을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to describe a very comfortable place.

phrases.example: 같은 일인데 사람에 따라 천당과 지옥이 돼요.
phrases.en: The same job can be heaven or hell depending on the people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 지옥과 짝으로 쓰는 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with its opposite, hell.

explain_en: It is the place religion says good people go after death, and its opposite is '지옥' (hell). People also say '천국', and in daily talk it can be a metaphor for a very comfortable, pleasant place.

examples.en: If you work out of sheer habit, your mistakes increase.

examples.ko: 오랜 타성에서 벗어나려고 새로운 방법을 시도했어요.
examples.en: I tried a new method to break free from my old rut.
Because of force of habit, I repeat the same mistake.
As my time at the company gets longer, I fall into a rut.
I changed jobs because I wanted to break out of my rut.
There's no fun in work you do just out of habit.

explain: 오래 해 와서 굳어져, 생각 없이 그냥 하게 되는 습관을 말해요. 대부분 나쁜 뜻이에요. 좋든 나쁘든 몸에 밴 '습관'과 달리, 변화 없이 매너리즘에 빠진 느낌이에요. '타성에 젖다', '타성에서 벗어나다' 같은 말과 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.example: 같은 일만 하다 보면 타성에 젖기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: If you only do the same work, it's easy to fall into a rut.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타성'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 말로, 변화 없이 습관처럼 하게 된다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with '타성', meaning doing things out of habit with no change.

phrases.example: 오랜 타성에서 벗어나려고 일하는 방법을 바꿨어요.
phrases.en: I changed how I work to get out of my long-standing rut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굳어진 습관에서 빠져나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting out of a fixed habit.

phrases.example: 새로운 취미가 타성을 깨는 데 도움이 됐어요.
phrases.en: A new hobby helped me break out of my rut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굳어진 습관을 일부러 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deliberately breaking a fixed habit.

explain_en: It means a habit that has set in over a long time and makes you act without thinking, and it is almost always negative. Unlike '습관', which can be good or bad, it carries a feeling of being stuck in a rut. It often appears in phrases such as '타성에 젖다' and '타성에서 벗어나다'.

examples.ko: 내일 발표인데 준비를 못 해서 걱정이 태산이에요.
examples.en: The presentation is tomorrow and I'm not ready, so I'm worried sick.

examples.ko: 할 일이 태산이라서 주말에도 쉬지 못해요.
examples.en: I have a mountain of work, so I can't rest even on weekends.
Things get worse and worse, just like the saying goes.
The laundry is piled up like a mountain, and I'm working late again today.

examples.ko: 태산처럼 쌓인 설거지를 보니 한숨이 나와요.
examples.en: I sigh when I see the mountain of dishes piled up.

examples.ko: 티끌 모아 태산이라고 매일 조금씩 저금해요.
examples.en: Little by little adds up, so I save a bit every day.

explain: 실제 큰 산보다 '걱정이 태산이다', '할 일이 태산이다'처럼 걱정이나 일이 아주 많다는 표현으로 더 자주 써요. '태산같이 쌓이다'처럼 비유로도 쓰고, 속담 '티끌 모아 태산'도 함께 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 이사 날짜는 다가오는데 짐을 못 쌌어요. 걱정이 태산이에요.
phrases.en: to be extremely worried
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이 아주 크고 많을 때 일상에서 흔히 쓰는 말이에요. 걱정 외에 '할 일이 태산이다'처럼도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday way to say your worries are huge. It also extends to things like '할 일이 태산이다' (a mountain of tasks).

phrases.example: 티끌 모아 태산이니까 커피값부터 아껴 볼게요.
phrases.en: small things add up to something big
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 것도 계속 모으면 크게 된다는 속담으로, 저금이나 노력을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb saying that small things add up if you keep collecting them, often used about saving money or effort.

explain_en: Rather than meaning an actual huge mountain, it is more often used in expressions like '걱정이 태산이다' (worried sick) and '할 일이 태산이다' (a mountain of work). It also works as a metaphor, and the proverb '티끌 모아 태산' is worth knowing too.

examples.ko: 그는 늦잠 잔 걸 교통 탓으로 합리화해요.
examples.en: He rationalizes oversleeping by blaming the traffic.
If you rationalize your own mistakes, it's hard to improve.

examples.ko: 비싼 옷을 산 걸 세일이었다고 합리화했어요.
examples.en: I justified buying the expensive clothes by saying they were on sale.

examples.ko: 회사는 업무 절차를 합리화하려고 새 시스템을 도입했어요.
examples.en: The company introduced a new system to make its work procedures more rational.

examples.ko: 운동 안 하는 걸 바빠서라고 합리화하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't excuse not exercising by saying you're busy.
Rationalizing it like that won't make the problem go away.

explain: '변명하다'와 비슷하지만, 스스로 옳다고 믿으려고 이유를 만들어 붙이는 느낌이 강해요. 사람이 주어이면 대개 좋지 않게 들리고 '자기 합리화'라는 말도 자주 써요. 회사나 제도가 대상이면 '효율적으로 바꾸다'에 가까워서 나쁜 느낌이 없어요.

phrases.en: He kept making excuses for being late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '합리화하다'와 비슷하지만 다른 사람에게 말하는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 합리화하다, but it focuses more on telling others.

phrases.en: That's nothing but self-justification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 옳다고 믿으려 할 때 쓰는 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for trying to convince oneself one is right.

phrases.en: Don't rationalize your mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 충고할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the negative when giving advice.

explain_en: It is close to '변명하다' (make excuses), but stronger in the sense of building reasons so that you can believe you were right. With a person as the subject it usually sounds negative, and '자기 합리화' (self-justification) is a common phrase. With a company or system as the object it is closer to 'make more efficient' and carries no negative tone.
